expectedFacts: HttpRequestParser::parseRequest compares the declared content length to getClientMaxBodySize and returns 413 (HttpRequestParser.cc:277-279); the chunked path adds each chunk length to the running total and returns 413 when over the same limit (:380-382).
HttpRequestImpl::decompressBodyGzip stops with TooLarge when the expanded output exceeds getClientMaxBodySize (HttpRequestImpl.cc:1040); HttpServer's tryDecompressRequest turns that status into 413.
HttpServer::onRequests stops the parser and shuts the connection down when the number of requests parsed on it reaches the keep-alive request limit (HttpServer.cc:333-339).
HttpServer::onRequests applies the same shutdown when queued pipelined requests plus the new batch reach the pipelining limit (HttpServer.cc:341-347).

HttpConnectionLimit::tryAddConnection (called from HttpServer::onConnection) refuses a new connection when the global count before it already exceeds the global maximum (fetch_add returns the old count, so one extra connection is admitted) or when the per-IP count exceeds the per-IP maximum; the server then force-closes it (HttpConnectionLimit.cc:30-54, HttpServer.cc:121-125).
WebSocketMessageParser::parse rejects a masked (client) frame whose length exceeds getClientMaxWebSocketMessageSize (WebSocketConnectionImpl.cc:371-379).

r3hb-drogon-10.query: In a server-page template, a developer uses the placeholder form that takes only the name of a view-data entry, for an entry that the controller stored as a plain number with the general-purpose insert. The page renders with nothing at that spot, and no error is logged. Why does this happen, which code is responsible, and which other ways of putting a number on the page work?

expectedFacts: Session::changeSessionIdToClient only sets two flags (needToChange_ and needToSet_); it does not change the identifier at that moment (Session.h:220-224).

CRITICAL: HttpAppFrameworkImpl::handleSessionForResponse runs when the response is being sent. If the session needs a change it calls SessionManager::changeSessionId, then adds a session cookie with the new identifier (path '/', configured SameSite, max-age only when it is >= 0) to that response, using a temporary copy when the response is a shared cached object (HttpAppFrameworkImpl.cc:728-770).

SessionManager::changeSessionId gets the new identifier from the id-generator callback, inserts the same Session object under the new key (CacheMap::insert fires the session-start advice for the new key), and asks the session CacheMap to erase the old key with runAfter(10, ...) (SessionManager.cc:116-127; CacheMap.h:217-247).

CRITICAL: With a positive session timeout, the session CacheMap ticks once per second, so the old key stays about 10 seconds (low precision): a request carrying the old cookie still finds the same Session through getSession, and CacheMap::erase fires the session-destroy advice for the old identifier only when that delay ends (SessionManager.cc:31-67; CacheMap.h:387-396, 417-421).

With the default session timeout of 0 (sessions never expire), the session CacheMap is built with no tick and no wheels, so runAfter cannot schedule the task: the CallbackEntry is released at once and its destructor runs the erase immediately. The old identifier stops working at once (a request with it gets a new, empty session) and the destroy advice fires during handleSessionForResponse (SessionManager.cc:69-85; CacheMap.h:39-49, 417-421, 470-506).
